doc.title: Annie Ross interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2001

title: Writing words to 'Twisted' for Prestige
summary: Bob Weinstock of Prestige challenged her to put words to an instrumental; she wrote 'Twisted' (Wardell Gray's tune), recorded it and won a Down Beat New Star Award.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Tell me how the Farmer’s Market and that whole thing came about.

Well necessity is the mother of invention. And the necessity was the money. I knew George Wallington’s wife, who, you know he was the piano player with the Lionel Hampton band when I joined. He joined as well. And she took me down to see a man called Bob Weinstein [Weinstock], who owned Prestige Records, which was a very popular record label for young artists — Miles and people like that — who would be paid and who would sell their songs and be very happy to sell it because it meant money in the hand. I met him — “Moody’s Mood” had just come out. And he said to me, “do you know ‘Moody’s Mood’?” I said yes. He said, “do you think you could write words to an instrumental like Eddie Jefferson did?” Eddie having done “Moody’s Mood for Love” not King Pleasure. So I said yeah. I mean if you’d asked me if I could fly I would have said yes. So he said, “well here’s a pile of records, go back to your place, pick one, write the words, when you’re ready come to me.” Well I was living, I was sharing a floor, I had a room in this big building where you shared the kitchen, you shared the bathroom and it was — yuhlch. And so I was there the next morning with “Twisted.”
Is that right?
Yeah.
That’s amazing. © Fillius Jazz Archive -5-
I hurried up and wrote those words. I got out of that place.
And the tenor player — refresh my memory, was it Wardell Gray?
Wardell was the one who wrote the tune, yeah.
How did the initial —
Idea?
Idea come from that?

From the title. “Twisted.” What would that be? And then I looked at myself. When I write I write very fast. I’m very lazy. I really, you know, I should be much more productive than I am, I bide my time.
But when necessity —
Yeah, when necessity calls I really get to work.
So I guess Mr. Weinstein [Weinstock] liked it.
He was pretty surprised, yeah. And the next thing I knew we recorded it.
And it worked.

Well I recorded it and I left immediately for France. And while I was — no I didn’t leave for France, I went to Scotland to kind of see my family. And while I was there I was notified that I’d been awarded the New Star Award for Down Beat for doing “Twisted,” and I thought well that’s nice. But my mind wasn’t really that attuned to staying in America. And then I eventually came back and I started to get work which then led me to the Lionel Hampton band.
Okay, I had that backwards in my head. That “Twisted” came before the Hampton band.
Oh it did.
Yes, okay.
Oh yeah.
